android.desc: Radar Love Live Wallpaper is the battery-friendly live wallpaper that lets you view the current National Weather Service radar on your phone's background. Auto-location capability will select the nearest weather radar or you can manually select your station. Never get surprised by a storm again. With this app on your background there's no need to open any separate weather app to stay informed about your region's storms.

quotes.text:
They're also good for extremely bursty loads. I use Lambdas extensively for a radar imagery API that delivers the images for an Android live wallpaper that shows weather radar.

That particular use case can go from hardly any traffic at all to a hurricane of traffic during something like, well, a hurricane.

For consistent processing loads, I think I could save money by just running on dedicated EC2 instances, but you cannot beat the instant scale of Lambdas.

Shameless plug: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.radarlove.wallpaper

My very small team has built an Android live wallpaper that displays the current NEXRAD weather radar data as your Android phone’s live wallpaper.

The app automatically selects the nearest radar site using coarse location permissions, or you can manually choose a location. Everything is size optimized and only updates when the wallpaper is being viewed to minimize battery footprint.

Interesting technical bits:

  - Using the US National Weather Service public radar feed (via public S3 bucket)
  - Custom radar volume data decoder written in Go and running as AWS Lambdas (triggered by S3 bucket events)
  - Custom rendering API
  - Kotlin Android app is <10 MB (no cross-platform bloat)

Available on Google Play:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.radarlove.wallpaper&hl=en_US

Happy to answer questions about the radar data processing pipeline, infrastructure, or the live wallpaper implementation. Also open to interesting opportunities for collaboration...
